subject: Private patch exit strategy & timebox sync
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: AcmeHealth - EngOps <engops@acmehealth.com>, Procurement <procure@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private patch exit strategy & timebox sync

Hi team,

Thanks again for giving us the window to run the 1.24.3 → 1.25.0 maintenance on your private deployment next week. I wanted to align on the exit criteria and the precise timebox for the patch so we have clear rollback triggers and a communications cadence.

High-level proposal (attached spreadsheet):
- Maintenance window: 2026-09-02, 01:00–05:00 UTC (4h primary window + 1h observation)
- Canary: 2 control-plane nodes + 1 GPU pool (traffic routed to fallback cluster)
- Exit criteria (must all pass):
  - Post-upgrade health: all readiness probes green for 10 consecutive minutes
  - Latency: 95th percentile per-route latency not >20% above baseline for 15 minutes
  - Error budget: no increase in 5xx >1% for 30 minutes
  - KV cache warm-up: stable hit-rate back to baseline within 20 minutes
- Escape hatch: automatic rollback to 1.24.3 if ANY critical guard trips (see attached escape-hatch-checklist.pdf)

Questions for Acme ops: please confirm the proposed window fits your on-call shift and procurement SLA. Also confirm whether your network team will permit a brief IP failover test during the canary (we'll simulate a node drain).

Action items:
- Acme: confirm window and network permission by 2026-08-31 17:00 UTC
- Redwood: provide final runbook and DocuSign for maintenance authorization by 2026-08-31 20:00 UTC
- Both: quick dry-run (1h) on 2026-09-01 at 23:00 UTC if preferred

Attachments: 2026-08-30_acme_patch_timebox.xlsx (detailed sequence), escape-hatch-checklist.pdf

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

---

Note: If you need us to narrow the window to avoid your nightly backups, suggest a preferred 2-hour slot and we'll re-evaluate the canary size.

From: EngOps Team <engops@acmehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@acmehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private patch exit strategy & timebox sync

Neha —

Thanks for the clear plan. The proposed window (2026-09-02 01:00–05:00 UTC) is acceptable from our side; it avoids our nightly ETL and falls inside our change freeze exceptions.

A few confirmations/requests:
- Network: we can permit the IP failover test but only for 2 minutes on the canary nodes — we'll coordinate with our NOC and provide a point of contact (Alex Kim)
- Backups: we'll snapshot the control-plane and GPU volumes 30 minutes before the canary step starts (will not affect the window)
- Procurement: please include the standard maintenance addendum; we need the DocuSign link to start approval

Also: if there's a measurable cache warm-up regression, we prefer a staged unpin (back to 1.24.3 for the public endpoints only) before a full rollback — can Redwood support partial unpinning?

Regards,
Samira Patel
Engineering Operations Lead
AcmeHealth
engops@acmehealth.com

---

On Tue, 30 Aug 2026 at 12:30, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Heads up — quick internal alignment from Redwood before we lock the runbook.
> 
> From an ops-safety POV I'd propose tightening the canary window and adding two extra automated gates:
> 1) KV cache stability gate: if cache hit-rate falls >15% for 10m, pause continued rollout and revert only the routing (keep control-plane patched)
> 2) Token-cost regression gate: if tokens/second cost jumps >25% for 10m, auto-scale down the new pool and alert SRE
> 
> Proposed sequencing (detailed in the spreadsheet):
> - T-60m: snapshots + config freeze
> - T-30m: canary deploy to 2 nodes, 10m soak with synthetic traffic
> - T+0m: if canary OK, fan out to 20% of GPU capacity for 30m with customer traffic split 90/10 (old/new)
> - T+30m: evaluate metrics, escalate if any gate trips; otherwise continue to 60% for 20m
> - T+60m: full fan-out and 1h observation
> 
> On partial unpin: yes, we can support route-level pinning. If Acme prefers partial rollback for public endpoints we can orchestrate a gradational rollback. Will note this in runbook.
> 
> Jonas Weber
> Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
> jonas_weber@redwood.com

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: EngOps Team <engops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private patch exit strategy & timebox sync

Perfect — thank you, Samira.

We will: 
- Narrow the canary control period to 10 minutes (per Jonas' suggestion) and include the KV cache and token-cost gates as automated checks in the runbook.
- Provide a DocuSign link for the maintenance addendum by 2026-08-31 20:00 UTC (Procurement: please watch for the email; it will contain the approved timebox and a single check-box for partial unpin permission).
- Confirm Alex Kim as the NOC contact for the 2-minute IP failover test and update the runbook to reflect the exact times.

Final note on rollback semantics: our escape-hatch checklist allows for two rollback flavors — "route rollback" (repoint specific customer routes back to 1.24.3) and "full fleet rollback" (complete revert of control-plane + GPU pools). We'll attempt route rollback first when possible to minimize customer impact.

Next steps:
- Redwood (Jonas, Monica) to produce runbook + automated gate definitions and upload to the shared drive link by EOD 2026-08-31.
- Acme (Samira/Procurement) to sign DocuSign by 2026-08-31 23:59 UTC.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments referenced above: 2026-08-30_acme_patch_timebox.xlsx, escape-hatch-checklist.pdf
